deck_name: Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot — The Lavish Outlier (c. 1442)

trump-emperor.name: The Emperor
trump-emperor.Scene: The Emperor of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot is a crowned male sovereign enthroned or standing against a gold-leaf background, painted by Bonifacio Bembo in the mid-15th century for the Visconti court of Milan. He wears the elaborate robes and armor of an Italian Renaissance ruler — likely reflecting the imagery of Filippo Maria Visconti or the early Sforza dynasty. The figure holds a scepter or orb, the attributes of temporal dominion, and is surrounded by the heraldic splendor of the ducal court. The gold ground and delicate tempera painting reflect the luxury production values of early tarot as an aristocratic gift object.

trump-empress.name: The Empress
trump-empress.Scene: The Empress of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot is a crowned imperial woman enthroned or standing against a gold-leaf background. She wears the elaborate courtly dress of a 15th-century Italian noblewoman, her regalia reflecting the prestige of the Visconti-Sforza family for whom this deck was painted. She holds the scepter or orb of female sovereignty, her presence the counterpart of the Emperor — temporal authority in its feminine expression. The gold ground and refined tempera technique by Bonifacio Bembo make this one of the most opulent representations of the Empress in tarot history.

trump-lovers.name: The Lovers
trump-lovers.Scene: The Lovers of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot shows a courtly scene of two figures — a man and a woman — in the act of a formal betrothal or amorous union, often with a Cupid or binding figure above. The image reflects the aristocratic culture of courtly love and dynastic marriage that characterized the Visconti-Sforza court. The gold-leaf background and the exquisite detail of the painted costumes make this card a document of the fashion and ceremony of 15th-century Milanese court life.

trump-chariot.name: The Chariot
trump-chariot.Scene: The Chariot of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot shows a victorious figure in a triumphal car — a chariot drawn by horses or other animals, the sovereign or allegorical figure riding above the world in a posture of victory. The image reflects the tradition of the Roman triumph (trionfi) which gave the tarot trumps their name, the allegorical pageant of victory that was a central feature of Italian Renaissance court celebration.

trump-strength.name: Strength
trump-strength.Scene: The Strength (Fortezza) of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot shows the allegorical virtue of Fortitude — possibly as a woman breaking a column or restraining a lion, the conventional iconography of this virtue in Italian medieval and Renaissance art. The Cary-Yale's Strength is one of three cardinal virtues surviving in this deck (alongside Faith, Hope, and Charity as theological virtues), making this an unusually virtue-rich early tarot.

trump-death.name: Death
trump-death.Scene: The Death card of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot shows the skeletal figure of Death as the universal harvester — though in the Cary-Yale's distinctive Bembo style, the figure is rendered with the technical refinement and dignity of aristocratic painting rather than the macabre grotesquerie of the danse macabre tradition. Against the gold ground, Death moves through the world as an allegorical presence from the same tradition as Petrarch's Triumph of Death.

trump-judgement.name: Judgement
trump-judgement.Scene: The Judgement of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot shows the angel of the Last Judgment sounding the trumpet above the risen dead — the conventional Christian eschatological scene rendered in the aristocratic style of 15th-century Milanese painting. The gold ground and fine tempera make this card a devotional object as much as a gaming piece, the divine judgment depicted with the reverence appropriate to a luxury commission for the Visconti court.

trump-world.name: The World
trump-world.Scene: The World of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot shows the cosmic completion of the triumph sequence — likely a figure or allegorical form representing the world as a whole, possibly with the mandorla (almond-shaped halo) that surrounds the feminine personification of the world in later Marseille tradition. The World is the apex of the surviving Cary-Yale trumps, the final triumph that crowns the allegorical sequence of the earliest surviving tarot deck.

virtue-faith.name: Faith
virtue-faith.Scene: Faith (Fede) is a theological virtue card unique to the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot — she does not appear as a separate trump in any standard later tarot deck. The figure of Faith is depicted as a woman with the attributes of Christian faith: possibly a chalice, a cross, or the Apostles' Creed scroll, or a figure holding a candle in darkness. Against the gold-leaf background of Bonifacio Bembo's luxury tempera painting, Faith stands as a theological complement to the three Cardinal Virtues (Fortitude, Justice, Temperance) that appear in most later tarots.

virtue-hope.name: Hope
virtue-hope.Scene: Hope (Speranza) is a theological virtue card unique to the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The figure of Hope is typically depicted as a woman with her hands raised toward heaven or reaching upward toward a divine anchor — the classical attributes of the virtue that sustains the soul in the absence of present certainty. Against the gold ground of the Bembo tempera, Hope stands as the second of the three theological virtues that distinguish this deck from all subsequent tarot traditions.

virtue-charity.name: Charity
virtue-charity.Scene: Charity (Carità) is the third theological virtue unique to the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot, completing the trio of faith, hope, and charity from the First Letter to the Corinthians. The figure of Charity is depicted as a woman in the act of giving — distributing gifts, nurturing children at her breast, or holding her heart toward others. Against the gold-leaf background of the Cary-Yale's luxury production, Charity is the virtue that grounds the theological trio in concrete action toward the other.

coins-ace.name: Ace of Coins
coins-ace.Scene: The Ace of Coins of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot shows a single large coin or disc against the card's field — the concentrated emblem of the suit in its undivided potential. The Cary-Yale's pip cards follow the Italian playing card tradition of showing suit symbols in simple geometric or heraldic arrangements, against the gold-touched or patterned backgrounds that reflect the deck's luxury production values.

coins-two.name: Two of Coins
coins-two.Scene: Two coins arranged in the card's field, showing the suit in its first act of division — the dyad that begins to structure the potential of the ace. In the Cary-Yale pip cards, the suit symbols are arranged in the simple geometric patterns inherited from the Italian playing card tradition, their elegant simplicity contrasting with the elaborate figurative work of the court cards.

coins-four.name: Four of Coins
coins-four.Scene: Four coins arranged in a square or cross pattern, the stable geometric foundation of the suit's middle range. The four of coins in the Cary-Yale reflects the conventional pip arrangement of the Italian playing card tradition, showing the suit symbol four times in a structured field.

coins-five.name: Five of Coins
coins-five.Scene: Five coins arranged in the card's field — the quincunx pattern (four corners and a center) that is a common arrangement in Italian pip cards. The five of coins in the Cary-Yale follows this convention, the suit symbol appearing five times in the playing card tradition's geometric ordering.

coins-six.name: Six of Coins
coins-six.Scene: Six coins arranged in two rows of three or three rows of two — the balanced abundance of the suit at six. The six of coins in the Cary-Yale follows the Italian playing card convention of arranging the suit symbol in even, orderly rows.

coins-seven.name: Seven of Coins
coins-seven.Scene: Seven coins arranged in an asymmetric or cross-and-row pattern, the suit at seven. The seven of coins in the Cary-Yale shows the suit symbol seven times in the playing card tradition's arrangement, the number seven marking the waiting point before the suit's final expansion toward ten.

coins-eight.name: Eight of Coins
coins-eight.Scene: Eight coins arranged in four rows of two or two rows of four — the even doubling of the suit at eight. The eight of coins in the Cary-Yale follows the Italian playing card tradition's geometric ordering, showing the suit symbol eight times in a structured field.

coins-nine.name: Nine of Coins
coins-nine.Scene: Nine coins arranged in three rows of three — the three-by-three square of the suit at nine, one step before completion. The nine of coins in the Cary-Yale shows the suit symbol nine times in the geometric pattern inherited from the Italian playing card tradition.

coins-ten.name: Ten of Coins
coins-ten.Scene: Ten coins arranged in rows or a pyramid pattern — the complete expression of the coins suit in its pip register. The ten of coins in the Cary-Yale is the apex of the pip arrangement, showing all ten instances of the suit symbol in the Italian playing card tradition's geometric ordering.

coins-damsel.name: Damsel of Coins
coins-damsel.Scene: The Damsel (Damigella) of Coins is one of the most distinctive features of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot — a young female court figure bearing the coin suit's emblem, corresponding to the male Knave (Fante) in later standard decks. The Cary-Yale's five-rank court system includes female figures at the lower ranks, reflecting the court culture of the Visconti-Sforza family. The Damsel is dressed in the elegant court attire of 15th-century Milan, a young noblewoman of the suit.

coins-knight.name: Knight of Coins
coins-knight.Scene: The Knight of Coins (Cavaliere di Denari) shows a mounted male figure bearing the coin suit's emblem — a knight on horseback in the armored court style of 15th-century Milan. The Cary-Yale's Knight follows the Italian playing card convention of the mounted court figure, his horse and armor reflecting the aristocratic military culture of the Visconti-Sforza court.

coins-horsewoman.name: Horsewoman of Coins
coins-horsewoman.Scene: The Horsewoman (Cavalleressa) of Coins is one of the most unusual court figures in tarot history — a female mounted figure bearing the coin suit's emblem, occupying the rank between the Damsel and the Queen in the Cary-Yale's distinctive five-rank court system. The Horsewoman reflects the court culture of the Visconti-Sforza family, where noblewomen occupied ceremonial and social positions of genuine prestige. She rides side-saddle or astride in the elegant dress of the Milanese court.

coins-queen.name: Queen of Coins
coins-queen.Scene: The Queen of Coins (Regina di Denari) is an enthroned female figure in the elaborate court dress of 15th-century Milan, bearing the coin suit's emblem. Against the gold-leaf background of the Cary-Yale's luxury tempera painting, the Queen of Coins represents the high feminine authority of the suit — the mistress of earthly resources, a figure who may reflect the actual queens and duchesses of the Visconti-Sforza court.

coins-king.name: King of Coins
coins-king.Scene: The King of Coins (Re di Denari) is an enthroned male figure in the elaborate regalia of a 15th-century Italian sovereign, bearing the coin suit's emblem. Against the gold-leaf background of the Cary-Yale's luxury production, the King of Coins is the apex of the suit's hierarchy — the master of earthly resources, a figure who may reflect the actual dukes of the Visconti-Sforza lineage for whom this deck was created.

cups-ace.name: Ace of Cups
cups-ace.Scene: The Ace of Cups shows a single ornate chalice or vase against the card's field — the concentrated emblem of the cups suit in its undivided potential. In the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot, the cup or vase is rendered in the style of 15th-century luxury metalwork, reflecting the court culture of Milan where actual gold and silver chalices were the objects of aristocratic prestige.

cups-two.name: Two of Cups
cups-two.Scene: Two cups in the card's field — the suit's first division, two chalices arranged in the simple bilateral symmetry of the Italian playing card tradition. The two of cups begins the suit's numerical expansion from the ace's concentrated potential.

cups-three.name: Three of Cups
cups-three.Scene: Three cups arranged in a triangular pattern — the triad of the suit at three. The three of cups in the Cary-Yale follows the playing card convention of showing the suit symbol three times in a geometric field.

cups-four.name: Four of Cups
cups-four.Scene: Four cups arranged in a square or cross pattern — the stable foundation of the suit at four. The four of cups shows the chalice emblem four times in the geometric arrangement of the Italian playing card tradition.

cups-five.name: Five of Cups
cups-five.Scene: Five cups arranged in the card's field — the quincunx or asymmetric arrangement of the suit at five. The five of cups shows the chalice five times in the playing card tradition's geometric ordering.

cups-six.name: Six of Cups
cups-six.Scene: Six cups in two or three rows — the balanced arrangement of the suit at six. The six of cups shows the chalice six times in the geometric field of the Italian playing card tradition.

cups-seven.name: Seven of Cups
cups-seven.Scene: Seven cups arranged in an asymmetric or cross-and-row pattern — the suit at seven, the waiting point before the final expansion toward ten. The seven of cups shows the chalice seven times in the playing card tradition's arrangement.

cups-eight.name: Eight of Cups
cups-eight.Scene: Eight cups in four pairs or two rows of four — the suit at eight, the even doubling of the chalice emblem. The eight of cups shows the cup eight times in the geometric field of the Italian playing card tradition.

cups-nine.name: Nine of Cups
cups-nine.Scene: Nine cups in three rows of three — the three-by-three arrangement of the suit at nine, one step before completion. The nine of cups shows the chalice nine times in the geometric pattern of the Italian playing card tradition.

cups-ten.name: Ten of Cups
cups-ten.Scene: Ten cups in rows or a pyramid arrangement — the completed expression of the cups suit. The ten of cups in the Cary-Yale shows the chalice ten times in the pip tradition's final geometric form.

cups-knave.name: Knave of Cups
cups-knave.Scene: The Knave (Fante) of Cups is a young male court figure bearing the cup suit's emblem, corresponding to the male page or knave of standard playing card traditions. In the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot, the Knave of Cups appears alongside the Damsel of Cups as part of the deck's expanded five-rank court system, a young man of the cups suit in the elegant dress of the 15th-century Milanese court.

cups-damsel.name: Damsel of Cups
cups-damsel.Scene: The Damsel (Damigella) of Cups is a young female court figure bearing the cup suit's emblem — a young noblewoman of the cups suit in the refined Bembo style, dressed in the elegant courtly attire of 15th-century Milan. As one of the Cary-Yale's unique female lower-court figures, the Damsel of Cups reflects the court culture of the Visconti-Sforza family where young women occupied positions of social prestige.

cups-knight.name: Knight of Cups
cups-knight.Scene: The Knight of Cups is a mounted male figure bearing the cup suit's emblem — a knight on horseback in the court armor of 15th-century Milan. The Knight of Cups brings the suit's emotional and aesthetic sensibility into active motion, the mounted courtier who carries the chalice into the world on horseback.

cups-king.name: King of Cups
cups-king.Scene: The King of Cups (Re di Coppe) is an enthroned male figure bearing the cup suit's emblem in the elaborate regalia of a 15th-century Italian sovereign. Against the gold-leaf background of the Cary-Yale's luxury tempera, the King of Cups represents the mature masculine authority of the suit — the master of emotional and aesthetic resources in the Visconti-Sforza court tradition.

swords-ace.name: Ace of Swords
swords-ace.Scene: The Ace of Swords shows a single upright sword against the card's field — the concentrated emblem of the suit in its undivided potential. In the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot, the sword is rendered in the style of 15th-century Italian arms, a refined blade rather than the crude weapon of popular imagery, reflecting the aristocratic context of the deck.

swords-two.name: Two of Swords
swords-two.Scene: Two swords in the card's field — the suit's first division, two blades arranged in the bilateral symmetry of the Italian playing card tradition. The two of swords begins the suit's numerical expansion.

swords-three.name: Three of Swords
swords-three.Scene: Three swords arranged in a triangular or vertical pattern — the suit at three. The three of swords shows the blade three times in the geometric field of the Italian playing card tradition.

swords-four.name: Four of Swords
swords-four.Scene: Four swords in a square or cross arrangement — the stable quadrant of the suit at four. The four of swords shows the blade four times in the geometric arrangement of the playing card tradition.

swords-five.name: Five of Swords
swords-five.Scene: Five swords in the card's field — the quincunx or asymmetric arrangement of the suit at five. The five of swords shows the blade five times in the playing card tradition's geometric ordering.

swords-six.name: Six of Swords
swords-six.Scene: Six swords in two or three rows — the even arrangement of the suit at six. The six of swords shows the blade six times in the geometric field of the Italian playing card tradition.

swords-seven.name: Seven of Swords
swords-seven.Scene: Seven swords in an asymmetric or cross-and-row pattern — the suit at seven, the waiting point before the final expansion. The seven of swords shows the blade seven times in the playing card tradition's arrangement.

swords-eight.name: Eight of Swords
swords-eight.Scene: Eight swords in four pairs or two rows of four — the even doubling of the blade emblem at eight. The eight of swords shows the sword eight times in the geometric field of the Italian playing card tradition.

swords-nine.name: Nine of Swords
swords-nine.Scene: Nine swords in three rows of three — the near-completion of the suit at nine. The nine of swords shows the blade nine times in the geometric pattern of the playing card tradition.

swords-ten.name: Ten of Swords
swords-ten.Scene: Ten swords in rows or a pyramid arrangement — the completed expression of the swords suit. The ten of swords in the Cary-Yale shows the blade ten times in the pip tradition's final geometric form.

swords-damsel.name: Damsel of Swords
swords-damsel.Scene: The Damsel of Swords is a young female court figure bearing the sword suit's emblem — a young noblewoman of the swords suit in the refined Bembo style, dressed in the elegant attire of 15th-century Milan. The Damsel of Swords is part of the Cary-Yale's unique five-rank court system, her presence reflecting the court culture of the Visconti-Sforza family.

swords-horsewoman.name: Horsewoman of Swords
swords-horsewoman.Scene: The Horsewoman of Swords is a female mounted figure bearing the sword suit's emblem — one of the Cary-Yale's most distinctive court figures. She rides in the elegant dress of the Milanese court, a noblewoman who occupies the mounted rank of the suit in the five-rank court system. The Horsewoman of Swords combines the refinement of the Bembo painting style with the martial emblem of the blade.

swords-queen.name: Queen of Swords
swords-queen.Scene: The Queen of Swords is an enthroned female figure bearing the sword suit's emblem in the elaborate dress of a 15th-century Italian noblewoman. Against the gold-leaf background of the Cary-Yale's luxury tempera, the Queen of Swords represents the high feminine authority of the suit — perhaps a duchess or lady of the Visconti-Sforza court, the clarity and precision of the blade expressed through aristocratic feminine power.

swords-king.name: King of Swords
swords-king.Scene: The King of Swords is an enthroned male figure bearing the sword suit's emblem in the elaborate regalia of a 15th-century Italian sovereign. Against the gold-leaf background of the Cary-Yale's luxury production, the King of Swords represents the mature masculine authority of the suit — the master of martial and intellectual power in the tradition of the Visconti-Sforza dukes of Milan.

batons-ace.name: Ace of Batons
batons-ace.Scene: The Ace of Batons (or Staves / Arrows as this deck sometimes renders them) shows a single staff, baton, or arrow against the card's field — the concentrated emblem of the suit in its undivided creative potential. The Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot uses a variable terminology for this suit, sometimes depicting what appear to be arrows rather than the rounded clubs of later Marseille tradition, reflecting the Italian playing card heritage of the early tarot.

batons-two.name: Two of Batons
batons-two.Scene: Two batons or arrows in the card's field — the suit's first division, the dyad of creative energy beginning its expansion. The two of batons shows the suit symbol twice in the bilateral arrangement of the Italian playing card tradition.

batons-three.name: Three of Batons
batons-three.Scene: Three batons or arrows in a triangular or vertical pattern — the suit at three. The three of batons shows the staff or arrow three times in the geometric arrangement of the Italian playing card tradition.

batons-four.name: Four of Batons
batons-four.Scene: Four batons or arrows in a square or cross arrangement — the stable foundation of the suit at four. The four of batons shows the staff four times in the geometric field of the Italian playing card tradition.

batons-five.name: Five of Batons
batons-five.Scene: Five batons or arrows in the card's field — the quincunx or asymmetric arrangement of the suit at five. The five of batons shows the staff five times in the playing card tradition's geometric ordering.

batons-six.name: Six of Batons
batons-six.Scene: Six batons or arrows in two or three rows — the balanced arrangement of the suit at six. The six of batons shows the staff six times in the geometric field of the Italian playing card tradition.

batons-seven.name: Seven of Batons
batons-seven.Scene: Seven batons or arrows in an asymmetric or cross-and-row pattern — the suit at seven, the waiting point before the final expansion toward ten. The seven of batons shows the staff seven times in the playing card tradition's arrangement.

batons-eight.name: Eight of Batons
batons-eight.Scene: Eight batons or arrows in four pairs or two rows of four — the even doubling of the staff emblem at eight. The eight of batons shows the baton eight times in the geometric field of the Italian playing card tradition.

batons-nine.name: Nine of Batons
batons-nine.Scene: Nine batons or arrows in three rows of three — the near-completion of the suit at nine. The nine of batons shows the staff nine times in the geometric pattern of the playing card tradition.

batons-ten.name: Ten of Batons
batons-ten.Scene: Ten batons or arrows in rows or a pyramid arrangement — the completed expression of the batons suit. The ten of batons in the Cary-Yale shows the staff or arrow ten times in the pip tradition's final geometric form.

batons-knave.name: Knave of Batons
batons-knave.Scene: The Knave (Fante) of Batons or Staves is a young male court figure bearing the baton suit's emblem — a young man of the suit in the elegant dress of the 15th-century Milanese court, rendered in the Bembo style against the gold-leaf background of the Cary-Yale's luxury production.

batons-damsel.name: Damsel of Batons
batons-damsel.Scene: The Damsel of Batons or Staves is a young female court figure bearing the baton suit's emblem — a young noblewoman of the creative suit in the refined Bembo style of the Cary-Yale. As one of the deck's unique female lower-court figures, the Damsel of Batons reflects the court culture of the Visconti-Sforza family where young women occupied positions of courtly prestige.

batons-horsewoman.name: Horsewoman of Batons
batons-horsewoman.Scene: The Horsewoman of Batons or Staves is a female mounted figure bearing the baton suit's emblem — one of the Cary-Yale's most remarkable court innovations. She rides in the elegant dress of the Milanese court, a noblewoman who occupies the mounted rank of the creative suit in the five-rank system that makes this deck unique in tarot history.

batons-queen.name: Queen of Batons
batons-queen.Scene: The Queen of Batons or Staves is an enthroned female figure bearing the baton suit's emblem in the elaborate dress of a 15th-century Italian noblewoman. Against the gold-leaf background of the Cary-Yale's luxury tempera, the Queen of Batons represents the high feminine authority of the creative suit — warmth, generosity, and creative power expressed through the aristocratic feminine ideal of the Visconti-Sforza court.

emg-surviving-trumps.name: The Surviving Trumps
emg-surviving-trumps.Scene: The surviving trumps of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot form an incomplete but historically precious group: Emperor, Empress, Lovers, Chariot, Strength, Death, Judgement, World — eight cards of what may have been eleven or more trumps in the original deck. These eight cards represent the earliest surviving evidence of the tarot allegorical sequence as a painted luxury object, commissioned for the Visconti-Sforza court of Milan in the mid-15th century.

emg-theological-virtues.name: The Theological Virtues — Faith, Hope, Charity
emg-theological-virtues.Scene: The three Theological Virtue cards (Faith, Hope, Charity) form a group unique to the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot among all surviving tarot decks. Placed alongside the Cardinal Virtues (Fortitude survives, while Justice and Temperance are among the lost cards), these three cards reflect the explicitly Christian devotional context of the earliest Milanese tarot. No later standard tarot deck includes these virtues as separate trump cards.

emg-suit-coins.name: Suit of Coins — with the Six-Rank Court
emg-suit-coins.Scene: The coins suit of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot comprises the surviving pip cards (ace, 2, 4-10; with the three apparently lost) and five court ranks: Damsel, Knight, Horsewoman, Queen, King. The suit is rendered in the refined Bembo tempera style against gold-leaf backgrounds, the round coin emblem repeated in geometric pip arrangements and held by aristocratic court figures.

emg-suit-cups.name: Suit of Cups — with the Six-Rank Court
emg-suit-cups.Scene: The cups suit of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot comprises the surviving pip cards (ace through ten) and four court ranks: Knave, Damsel, Knight, King. The ornate chalice emblem is shown in geometric pip arrangements and held by court figures in the refined Bembo style, the emotional and aesthetic suit rendered in the luxury tempera painting of mid-15th century Milan.

emg-suit-swords.name: Suit of Swords — with the Six-Rank Court
emg-suit-swords.Scene: The swords suit of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot comprises the surviving pip cards (ace through ten) and four court ranks: Damsel, Horsewoman, Queen, King. The blade emblem is shown in geometric pip arrangements and held by court figures including the unique Horsewoman, in the refined Bembo tempera style of the mid-15th century Milanese court.

emg-suit-batons.name: Suit of Batons — with the Six-Rank Court
emg-suit-batons.Scene: The batons suit of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot comprises the surviving pip cards (ace through ten) and four court ranks: Knave, Damsel, Horsewoman, Queen (with the King apparently lost). The staff or arrow emblem is shown in geometric pip arrangements and held by court figures including the unique Damsel and Horsewoman, in the refined Bembo style of the mid-15th century.

kw-pip.name: Pip
kw-pip.Scene: A keyword grouping of all pip cards (numbered ace through ten in each suit) in the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The pip cards of the Cary-Yale follow the Italian playing card convention of showing the suit symbol in geometric arrangements against the card's field — elegant and repetitive in their simplicity, contrasting with the elaborate figurative work of the court and trump cards.

kw-court-card.name: Court card
kw-court-card.Scene: A keyword grouping of all court cards across the four suits of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The court cards are the deck's most elaborate figurative work — kings and queens enthroned, knights and horsewomen mounted, damsels and knaves standing — all rendered in Bonifacio Bembo's refined tempera against gold-leaf grounds. The five-rank court system (King, Queen, Horsewoman, Knight, Damsel/Knave) is unique to the Cary-Yale among surviving tarot decks.

kw-air.name: Air
kw-air.Scene: A keyword grouping of items associated with the element of Air in the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot — the airy, mental, and communicative dimension of the suits. Air is traditionally associated with the swords suit: thought, speech, conflict, and the swift movement of mind through the world.

kw-bastoni.name: Bastoni
kw-bastoni.Scene: A keyword grouping using the Italian name 'Bastoni' for the batons or staves suit — the Italian playing card term for the suit of clubs or staves that corresponds to the wands suit in modern tarot. In the Cary-Yale, the bastoni appear as staffs, batons, or arrows.

kw-batons.name: Batons
kw-batons.Scene: A keyword grouping for the batons suit — the suit of staffs, clubs, or arrows that represents the creative, fiery, and enterprising dimension of the four suits. In the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot, the batons appear in various forms reflecting the Italian playing card heritage of the earliest tarot.

kw-coins.name: Coins
kw-coins.Scene: A keyword grouping for the coins suit — the suit of round discs or denari that represents the material, earthly, and financial dimension of the four suits. In the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot, the coins are depicted as refined circular emblems in the Italian playing card tradition.

kw-coppe.name: Coppe
kw-coppe.Scene: A keyword grouping using the Italian name 'Coppe' for the cups suit — the Italian playing card term for the cups that corresponds to the chalices or hearts of other card traditions. In the Cary-Yale, the coppe are ornate chalices reflecting the luxury metalwork culture of 15th-century Milan.

kw-cups.name: Cups
kw-cups.Scene: A keyword grouping for the cups suit — the suit of chalices or vases that represents the emotional, intuitive, and aesthetic dimension of the four suits. In the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot, the cups are rendered as ornate luxury chalices appropriate to the court context of the deck's creation.

kw-denari.name: Denari
kw-denari.Scene: A keyword grouping using the Italian name 'Denari' for the coins suit — the Italian playing card term for the round coins or discs. Denari is the original Italian name for this suit, derived from the Roman denarius, the coin of everyday commerce and aristocratic wealth alike.

kw-earth.name: Earth
kw-earth.Scene: A keyword grouping for items associated with the element of Earth in the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot — the material, stable, and productive dimension of the suits. Earth is traditionally associated with the coins suit: the physical world, material resources, and the patient accumulation of earthly goods.

kw-fire.name: Fire
kw-fire.Scene: A keyword grouping for items associated with the element of Fire in the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot — the creative, passionate, and enterprising dimension of the suits. Fire is traditionally associated with the batons suit: energy, enthusiasm, and the spark that initiates creative endeavors.

kw-spade.name: Spade
kw-spade.Scene: A keyword grouping using the Italian name 'Spade' for the swords suit — the Italian playing card term for the swords or spades. Spade is the original Italian name for this suit, the blade as the emblem of mental clarity, conflict, and the cutting away of what is false.

kw-swords.name: Swords
kw-swords.Scene: A keyword grouping for the swords suit — the suit of blades that represents the mental, communicative, and conflictual dimension of the four suits. In the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot, the swords are rendered as refined blades appropriate to the aristocratic military culture of 15th-century Milan.

kw-water.name: Water
kw-water.Scene: A keyword grouping for items associated with the element of Water in the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot — the emotional, intuitive, and fluid dimension of the suits. Water is traditionally associated with the cups suit: feeling, imagination, and the receptive depth of the inner life.

kw-cary-yale.name: Cary-yale
kw-cary-yale.Scene: A keyword grouping identifying all items belonging to the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot — the deck commissioned for the Visconti-Sforza court of Milan c. 1441-1447, painted by Bonifacio Bembo, and now held at the Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library at Yale University. The Cary-Yale is one of three related Visconti-Sforza decks (with the Visconti di Modrone and the Pierpont-Morgan-Bergamo), and is the earliest of the three in its stylistic dating.

kw-trump.name: Trump
kw-trump.Scene: A keyword grouping for all trump cards in the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot — the allegorical major arcana cards that represent the trionfi tradition of Italian Renaissance pageantry. Of the original Cary-Yale trumps, eight survive (Emperor, Empress, Lovers, Chariot, Strength, Death, Judgement, World) plus the three Theological Virtues that are unique to this deck.

kw-ace.name: Ace
kw-ace.Scene: A keyword grouping for all aces across the four suits of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The aces are the concentrated emblems of each suit in its undivided potential — a single coin, a single cup, a single sword, a single baton — the seeds from which the numerical expansion of each suit grows.

kw-damsel.name: Damsel
kw-damsel.Scene: A keyword grouping for all Damsel (Damigella) court figures across the suits of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The Damsel is a young female court figure unique to the Cary-Yale's five-rank court system, occupying the lowest female rank in each suit's hierarchy and representing the young noblewomen of the Visconti-Sforza court.

kw-eight.name: Eight
kw-eight.Scene: A keyword grouping for all eight-pip cards across the suits of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The eights show each suit symbol eight times in the geometric arrangement of the Italian playing card tradition, representing the even doubling of the suit's potential at the register of competent accumulation.

kw-five.name: Five
kw-five.Scene: A keyword grouping for all five-pip cards across the suits of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The fives show each suit symbol five times, the mid-point disruption of the suit's numerical expansion, the quincunx or asymmetric arrangement that tips toward challenge or change.

kw-four.name: Four
kw-four.Scene: A keyword grouping for all four-pip cards across the suits of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The fours show each suit symbol four times in the stable geometric arrangement of the Italian playing card tradition — the quadrant of stable foundation.

kw-nine.name: Nine
kw-nine.Scene: A keyword grouping for all nine-pip cards across the suits of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The nines show each suit symbol nine times in the three-by-three arrangement of the Italian playing card tradition, the near-completion of each suit's numerical range.

kw-seven.name: Seven
kw-seven.Scene: A keyword grouping for all seven-pip cards across the suits of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The sevens show each suit symbol seven times in the asymmetric or cross-and-row arrangement of the Italian playing card tradition, the patient waiting point before the suit's final expansion.

kw-six.name: Six
kw-six.Scene: A keyword grouping for all six-pip cards across the suits of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The sixes show each suit symbol six times in the even-row arrangement of the Italian playing card tradition, representing the balanced abundance of each suit at its orderly double-register.

kw-ten.name: Ten
kw-ten.Scene: A keyword grouping for all ten-pip cards across the suits of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The tens show each suit symbol ten times in the final pyramid or row arrangement of the Italian playing card tradition, the completed expression of each suit's numerical range.

kw-two.name: Two
kw-two.Scene: A keyword grouping for all two-pip cards across the suits of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The twos show each suit symbol twice in the bilateral arrangement of the Italian playing card tradition, representing the first division of each suit's concentrated potential.

kw-horsewoman.name: Horsewoman
kw-horsewoman.Scene: A keyword grouping for all Horsewoman (Cavalleressa) court figures across the suits of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The Horsewoman is a female mounted court figure unique to the Cary-Yale's five-rank court system, occupying the mounted rank alongside or instead of the male Knight, and representing one of the most historically unusual court figures in the entire history of playing cards and tarot.

kw-king.name: King
kw-king.Scene: A keyword grouping for all King court figures across the suits of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The Kings are enthroned male figures bearing each suit's emblem in the elaborate regalia of 15th-century Italian sovereignty, rendered in Bonifacio Bembo's luxury tempera against gold-leaf grounds.

kw-queen.name: Queen
kw-queen.Scene: A keyword grouping for all Queen court figures across the suits of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The Queens are enthroned female figures bearing each suit's emblem in the elaborate dress of 15th-century Italian noblewomen, rendered in Bonifacio Bembo's luxury tempera against gold-leaf grounds.

kw-theological-virtue.name: Theological virtue
kw-theological-virtue.Scene: A keyword grouping for the three Theological Virtue trump cards (Faith, Hope, Charity) that are unique to the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The theological virtues of the Pauline epistles (1 Corinthians 13) are represented as separate allegorical trump figures alongside the Cardinal Virtues — a feature that distinguishes the Cary-Yale from every other surviving tarot deck and reflects the explicitly Christian devotional context of the earliest Milanese tarot.

kw-three.name: Three
kw-three.Scene: A keyword grouping for all three-pip cards across the suits of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot. The threes show each suit symbol three times in the triangular or vertical arrangement of the Italian playing card tradition, representing the first triangular expansion of each suit's potential. Note that the three of coins does not appear to survive in the Cary-Yale.

axis-keyword.name: By Keyword
axis-keyword.Scene: The keyword axis of the Cary-Yale Visconti Tarot organizes the deck's 105 items by thematic grouping — suits, elements, pip numbers, court ranks, and special categories (trumps, theological virtues, the deck's unique features). This axis allows navigation across the deck through the conceptual patterns that cut across the suit and trump organization, revealing the structural principles of the earliest surviving luxury tarot.
